tagline: Local encrypted clipboard history for macOS
verdictSummary: A clipboard history manager — keep the last N things you copied, searchable, pin the ones you reuse — is a small, well-scoped one-sitting build on macOS. What's genuinely harder to reproduce: iCloud sync across devices, rich previews for every content type, and years of edge-case handling for apps with unusual clipboard behavior.
coreLoopDIY: Poll the system pasteboard for changes, store each new clipboard entry locally with a timestamp and source app, and surface a searchable, pinnable history through a global hotkey.
whatYouLose: iCloud sync across Mac, iPhone, and iPad
rich previews for every file and color type
whyPeopleStillPay: The clipboard-history loop itself is simple; what's hard to fake is polish across every possible thing someone might copy, and having it just work identically on every Apple device.
prompt: Build a macOS menu-bar clipboard-history manager. Poll NSPasteboard's change count (or use a lightweight polling loop) to detect new clipboard content, and store each entry — text, image, or file reference — locally in SQLite with a timestamp, source app name, and content type. Show history through a global hotkey (e.g. Cmd+Shift+V) as a searchable, keyboard-navigable list; pressing enter re-copies the selected entry to the pasteboard. Support pinning entries to a persistent pinboard that survives history expiration, and an expiration setting (e.g. auto-delete plain-text entries after N days, keep pinned ones forever). Encrypt the local SQLite database at rest using a key held in the macOS Keychain. Add a basic preview pane for text and images. Do not build iCloud sync, cross-device support, or a plugin system for third-party format handlers — those are out of scope. No account or API key needed; everything is local.

faq.a: It stays local and encrypted at rest with a key from the macOS Keychain — nothing is sent anywhere, since there's no sync feature in this build to send it through.

faq.q: Will it capture passwords I copy from a password manager?
faq.a: Yes, by default, since it watches the system pasteboard indiscriminately — add your password manager to an exclusion list, or manually clear sensitive entries, since automatic detection isn't built in here.

faq.q: Does it sync between my Mac and iPhone?
faq.a: No — that's the main thing this build gives up. Paste's iCloud sync across devices is real engineering this prompt doesn't attempt.

faq.q: How far back does the history go?
faq.a: As far as your configured retention setting and disk space allow — there's no hard cap beyond what you set, unlike some clipboard managers with fixed history limits.
